requirements.quote:
endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to receiving a packet
   that it cannot associate with an active connection.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet that it cannot associate with an active connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send a Stateless Reset in response.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-to-connection association failure and the resulting response can be observed.

requirements.quote:
connections.  An endpoint that wishes to communicate a fatal
   connection error MUST use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame if it is able.
requirements.condition: An endpoint is able to send a frame and wishes to communicate a fatal connection error.
requirements.required_behavior: It must use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not use a Stateless Reset instead to communicate that active-connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can induce a fatal error on an active connection and inspect the emitted frame.

requirements.quote:

requirements.condition: An endpoint issues a stateless reset token.
requirements.required_behavior: The token must be 16 bytes long.
requirements.why_checkable: The issued token length is directly measurable.

requirements.quote:
To support this process, an endpoint issues a stateless reset token,
   which is a 16-byte value that is hard to guess.  If the peer
requirements.condition: An endpoint generates a stateless reset token.
requirements.required_behavior: The generated value must be hard to guess.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not use predictably generated token values.
requirements.why_checkable: Token generation and its entropy source can be inspected or statistically tested.

requirements.quote:
subsequently receives a Stateless Reset, which is a UDP datagram that
   ends in that stateless reset token, the peer will immediately end the
   connection.
requirements.condition: A peer receives a UDP datagram ending in the stateless reset token associated with its connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The peer must immediately end the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The peer must not continue the connection after recognizing the Stateless Reset.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection state can be observed immediately after delivery of a matching datagram.

requirements.quote:
A stateless reset token is specific to a connection ID.  An endpoint
   issues a stateless reset token by including the value in the
   Stateless Reset Token field of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.  Servers
requirements.condition: An endpoint issues a stateless reset token through a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The token must be specific to the connection ID and placed in the frame's Stateless Reset Token field.
requirements.why_checkable: The token-to-connection-ID association and encoded frame field can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
can also issue a stateless_reset_token transport parameter during the
   handshake that applies to the connection ID that it selected during
   the handshake.  These exchanges are protected by encryption, so only
requirements.condition: A server issues a stateless_reset_token transport parameter during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The parameter must apply to the connection ID selected by the server during that handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake state can be correlated with the transport parameter and selected connection ID.

requirements.quote:
handshake.  These exchanges are protected by encryption, so only
   client and server know their value.  Note that clients cannot use the
   stateless_reset_token transport parameter because their transport
   parameters do not have confidentiality protection.
requirements.condition: A client sends its transport parameters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not use the stateless_reset_token transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's encoded transport parameters can be inspected for presence of this parameter.

requirements.quote:
Tokens are invalidated when their associated connection ID is retired
   via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame (Section 19.16).
requirements.condition: A connection ID is retired via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The stateless reset token associated with that connection ID must be invalidated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The retired connection ID's token must not remain valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Token validity can be tested before and after processing the retirement frame.

requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs a Stateless Reset packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The first two fixed bits must have value 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The first two packet bits can be decoded and compared with the fixed value.

requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs a Stateless Reset packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Unpredictable Bits field must contain at least 38 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width can be calculated from the encoded datagram.

requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs a Stateless Reset packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset Token field must contain exactly 128 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The trailing token field's encoded width is directly measurable.

requirements.quote:
A Stateless Reset uses an entire UDP datagram, starting with the
   first two bits of the packet header.  The remainder of the first byte
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a Stateless Reset.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset must occupy the entire UDP datagram and start with the first two bits of the packet header.
requirements.why_checkable: UDP payload boundaries and packet-bit placement can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
first two bits of the packet header.  The remainder of the first byte
   and an arbitrary number of bytes following it are set to values that
   SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.  The last 16 bytes of the
requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs the non-token portion of a Stateless Reset.
requirements.required_behavior: The remainder of the first byte and following unpredictable bytes should be indistinguishable from random.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Those bytes should not contain a distinguishable deterministic pattern.
requirements.why_checkable: Generation logic and output distributions can be inspected or statistically tested.

requirements.quote:
SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.  The last 16 bytes of the
   datagram contain a stateless reset token.
requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs a Stateless Reset datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: The final 16 bytes must contain the stateless reset token.
requirements.why_checkable: The datagram suffix can be compared with the expected token.

requirements.quote:
to appear as a valid QUIC packet, the Unpredictable Bits field needs
   to include at least 38 bits of data (or 5 bytes, less the two fixed
   bits).
requirements.condition: A Stateless Reset is constructed to appear as a valid QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Its Unpredictable Bits field must include at least 38 bits of data.
requirements.why_checkable: The unpredictable field's length is directly measurable.

requirements.quote:
the endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22
   bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length that it requests
   the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as
   necessary.
requirements.condition: An endpoint requests a minimum connection ID length from its peer.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint should make every packet it sends at least 22 bytes longer than that requested minimum connection ID length, adding PADDING frames when necessary.
requirements.why_checkable: Sent packet lengths can be compared with the requested minimum connection ID length.

requirements.quote:
endpoint that sends a Stateless Reset in response to a packet that is
   43 bytes or shorter SHOULD send a Stateless Reset that is one byte
   shorter than the packet it responds to.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a Stateless Reset in response to a packet of 43 bytes or less.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset should be exactly one byte shorter than the triggering packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The response and triggering packet lengths can be compared.

requirements.quote:
unpredictable bytes are necessary if the endpoint could have
   negotiated a packet protection scheme with a larger minimum
   expansion.
requirements.condition: The endpoint could have negotiated a packet-protection scheme whose minimum expansion exceeds the stateless reset token length.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset must contain additional unpredictable bytes sufficient to account for the larger minimum expansion.
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated scheme's minimum expansion and the encoded unpredictable-byte count can be compared.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send a Stateless Reset that is three times or
   more larger than the packet it receives to avoid being used for
   amplification.
requirements.condition: An endpoint considers sending a Stateless Reset in response to a received packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not send a Stateless Reset whose size is at least three times the size of the received packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The sizes of the triggering packet and response datagram can be measured and compared.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MUST discard packets that are too small to be valid QUIC
   packets.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet that is too small to be a valid QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must discard the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not process the packet as valid QUIC.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver an undersized packet and observe whether it is discarded.

requirements.quote:
packets.  To give an example, with the set of AEAD functions defined
   in [QUIC-TLS], short header packets that are smaller than 21 bytes
   are never valid.
requirements.condition: The endpoint uses the set of AEAD functions defined in QUIC-TLS and receives a short-header packet smaller than 21 bytes.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet must be classified as invalid and discarded under the preceding rule.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not accept the packet as valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet form and length are directly controllable, and acceptance or discard is observable.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MUST send Stateless Resets formatted as a packet with a
   short header.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a Stateless Reset.
requirements.required_behavior: It must format the Stateless Reset as a short-header packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not send the Stateless Reset formatted with a long header.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted packet's header form can be decoded.

requirements.quote:
short header.  However, endpoints MUST treat any packet ending in a
   valid stateless reset token as a Stateless Reset, as other QUIC
   versions might allow the use of a long header.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives any packet ending in a valid stateless reset token.
requirements.required_behavior: It must treat the packet as a Stateless Reset regardless of whether its header is short or long.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: It must not reject Stateless Reset recognition solely because the packet lacks a short header.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets with differing header forms but the same valid token suffix can be supplied and classification observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to a packet with a
   long header.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet with a long header.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send a Stateless Reset in response.
requirements.why_checkable: A long-header input can be supplied and the optional response observed.

requirements.quote:
version, packets with a long header are only used during connection
   establishment.
requirements.condition: A packet uses a long header in this QUIC version.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet must be used only during connection establishment.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Long-header packets must not be used after connection establishment.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet header form can be correlated with the connection-establishment state.

requirements.quote:
stateless reset token being available to a peer.  In this QUIC
   version, packets with a long header are only used during connection
   establishment.  Because the stateless reset token is not available
   until connection establishment is complete or near completion,
requirements.condition: Connection establishment is not complete or near completion.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The stateless reset token must not yet be available to the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: Token availability can be correlated with the connection-establishment phase.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint cannot determine the Source Connection ID from a packet
   with a short header; therefore, it cannot set the Destination
   Connection ID in the Stateless Reset.  The Destination Connection ID
   will therefore differ from the value used in previous packets.
requirements.condition: An endpoint constructs a Stateless Reset in response to a short-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset's Destination Connection ID must differ from the value used in previous packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not derive and set the Destination Connection ID from a Source Connection ID in the short-header packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The response Destination Connection ID can be compared with connection IDs in earlier packets.
